packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-05 -- unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading. I did list the packet directory (file names/sizes only) and read image pixel dimensions with sips; I did not open packet.json.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview, recto face)
- A narrow vertical strip of parchment (c. 4.5 cm wide x c. 33 cm tall by the ruler), cut from a larger single sheet; text runs horizontally across the strip, so only a short middle/right part of each long line survives (left and right ends of lines are lost at both cut edges). Pencil shelfmark at foot: "Stams, Stft, Frg. 59r" (modern).
- One block of text, c. 33 lines, no columns, no ruling visible at this scale. Cursive documentary hand in a vernacular (German) language, long-shafted s/f descenders. Looks like a charter/deed (document prose: "erben", "bezalt", "nach dato ditz brie(fs)"), not a codex leaf. Observation: below the text a large looped flourish/notarial-style or signature mark ("S" in an oval) at c. y 820-860; lower third blank. Hole at top (stitching/ fold?). No rubrics, no initials, no glosses visible.
- Tiles 002-004 appear to be native-resolution vertical tiles of this face; image-005 the second (verso?) overview with tiles 006-008.

TRANSCRIPTION

== image-002 (top tile of recto strip; lines cut at left and right edges) ==
Notes: small open "c"-like mark over u = u-diacritic, rendered ů. "[..]" = text lost at the cut edge (not illegible).
image-002 l.1: [..]ell mein erben dat? ich [..]
image-002 l.2: [..]w(ů?)ssentlich vnd in [..]
image-002 l.3: [..]orffe? . macht haben so? [..]
image-002 l.4: [..]den erben ůnnante? / vntnante? [..]
image-002 l.5: [..]d strass Gegen mit(t)[..]
image-002 l.6: [..]en mannmadt wisen [..]
image-002 l.7: [..]r den genante(n) stra[..]
image-002 l.8: [..]nd vnerband? be suer? [..]  (a slot/hole before "vnerband")
image-002 l.9: [..]r zů gehort vnd [..]
image-002 l.10: [..]marckh zal perner [..]
image-002 l.11: [..]von den gemelten [..]
image-002 l.12: [..]vnnd bezalt sein an[..]
image-002 l.13: [..]ung? Dros? / drůs? mein f[..]
image-002 l.14: [..]r erben hendt ge[..]
image-002 l.15: [..]em obemelte(n) land[..]
image-002 l.16: [..]n hůsfrean? (= hausfrauen?) erw?[..]
image-002 l.17: (cut at tile foot; continues in image-003)

== image-003 (middle/lower tile of recto; lines 1-4 overlap image-002 l.13-16, not new text) ==
image-003 l.1: [..]ung? Dros? / Drůs? mein f[..]   (= image-002 l.13)
image-003 l.2: [..]r erben hendt ge[..]   (= image-002 l.14)
image-003 l.3: [..]em obemelte(n) land[..]   (= image-002 l.15)
image-003 l.4: [..]n hůsfrean? erw?[..]   (= image-002 l.16)
image-003 l.5: [..] damit handlen v[..]
image-003 l.6: [..]kumbt? . An alle [..]   (first word could be "krumbt"; long-s/k at left edge)
image-003 l.7: [..]v? vnnd darumb au[..]
image-003 l.8: [..]glich(e)d? wie s?thiemen? [..]   (third word very uncertain: long s + "thiemen"/"ihnen"?)
image-003 l.9: [..]s offt vnd? / nid? ders? / des not [..]
image-003 l.10: [..]ff zů recht nertig? / nottig? [..]
image-003 l.11: [..] nach dato ditz brie[f..]
image-003 l.12: [..] von kamem? / kainem? vnde[..]
image-003 l.13: [..]ů? male? alle sa[..]
image-003 l.14: [..]renne? erben anst[..]
image-003 l.15: [..]ief Behalt? / Beholt? m[..]
image-003 l.16: [..] / beuelch vmb da[..]
image-003 l.17: [..] wider dar? ni[..]
image-003 l.18: [..]l pondl? tassar? b[..]
image-003 l.19: [..]effen am Stambs? / stambs? [..]
image-003 l.20: [..]erntzehenden? (read "erntzecsenden"; probably -tzehenden, the numeral ending) [..]
Note: line 20 appears to be the last line of text; image-001 shows the looped "S" mark below it.

== image-004 (foot of recto; lines 1-3 overlap image-003 l.18-20, no new text) ==
image-004 l.1-3 = image-003 l.18-20. At higher zoom l.3 reads [..]erntzehenden? / ernntzechenden? with ů-type mark over the "n" after "er"; a tall stroke (long s or similar descender from line above) crosses it.
Below: a looped mark: capital "S" inside a large oval loop with a flourish continuing off the right cut edge (signature/notarial or scribe's mark - observation only). Rest of strip blank, with fold lines (horizontal and vertical crease). Pencil modern note: "Stams, STA, Frg. 59r" (correcting my survey's "Stft").

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-005, overview, verso face)
- Same strip photographed lying horizontally (rotated 90 degrees). Pencil note at right end, reading "Stams, StA, Frg. 59v". Surface appears blank of ink text at this scale; faint show-through of the recto writing, fold creases, small holes, one ink/dark mark near left end (c. x 290). A uniform grey rectangle masks the middle portion (c. x 430-650) - an applied mask in the image, not the object; whatever is under it is not visible.
- Tiles 006-008 presumably cover this face at native resolution.

== image-006 (verso, left third) ==
No ink text. The dark marks are holes/slits in the parchment (a slit near top centre, a hole at left on the crease, two small pinholes on the horizontal fold). Only faint show-through of recto strokes; nothing transcribable. Grey mask begins at right edge.

== image-007 (verso, middle) ==
No ink text visible. Grey mask covers lower-left/centre area (c. x 180-1065, y 315-760); content beneath unknown. Small faint grey-blue smudge above the mask (c. x 450-520, y 215) - pencil or stain, not readable. Right half shows only show-through of recto letters (mirror-reversed, faint), creases, two pinholes.

== image-008 (verso, right third) ==
No ink text. Modern pencil at right end, written along the strip: "Stams, StA, Frg. 59v". Fold creases, pinholes, faint show-through only.

LIMITATIONS / SUMMARY
- Recto: 20 lines of a vernacular (German, Upper German spelling: "marckh", "perner", "beuelch", "vnnd", u-diacritic ů) documentary text, all read but every line is a short middle segment of a much longer line; both line-ends lost at the cut edges, so no sentence is complete. Content-level observations only: heirs ("erben"), a meadow measure ("mannmadt wisen"), road ("strass"), payment ("zal perner", "bezalt"), "nach dato ditz brie[f]", "beuelch", "am Stambs?" (l.19, uncertain), dating-clause numeral ending "-tzehenden?" in the last line. Followed by a looped "S" mark.
- Most uncertain readings: image-002 l.4 (ůnnante/vntnante), l.8 (vnerband be suer), l.13 (Dros/drůs), l.16 (hůsfrean); image-003 l.8 (s?thiemen), l.9, l.10, l.12, l.15, l.18 (pondl tassar), l.19 (Stambs).
- Verso: blank apart from the pencil shelfmark; a grey mask in images 005/007 hides part of the verso (centre), so anything under it (endorsement?) is unread.
- No crops were made. I did nothing beyond the brief other than listing the packet directory and reading image dimensions with sips. No identification was revealed to me.
